title: Beyond the Superintelligent Machine: A Systems Definition of Superintelligence for the Era of Agentic AI
content: Superintelligence is usually defined as a machine intellect that exceeds human cognition across most domains. That framing conflates three distinct properties: computational capability, warranted knowledge, and legitimate authority. This article develops a systems definition suited to large language models, tool-using agents, databases, theorem provers, and other computational knowledge artifacts. Using conceptual synthesis and constructive requirement derivation, we distinguish a computational artifact, an operational self that preserves commitments and consequence history, and a normative principal that holds purpose and accountability. Human-created programs, proofs, databases, and learned models can embody accumulated knowledge and recorded consequences without phenomenal experience; what converts stored information into operationally discernible knowledge is provenance, validation, consequence closure, and revisability. We define superintelligence as a property of a constitutionally governed human-machine system that applies knowledge beyond unaided human scale, speed, or reliability within a declared scope while preserving human-ratified purpose, independently bounded authority for consequential action, authoritative memory, and ratified learning from outcomes. Eight architectural properties and falsifiable evaluation criteria are derived. Published Mindful Machine implementations are used as constructive feasibility evidence, while current regulatory and runtime-governance frameworks delimit what remains to be demonstrated.
